name: Curcumin

lead: Curcumin is the main yellow polyphenol of turmeric (Curcuma longa). It is widely sold as a supplement and used in cooking and traditional medicine.

In recovery and appearance contexts it is taken for joint soreness, general inflammation and skin health. Systematic reviews report modest benefits for arthritis symptoms and inflammatory markers, though trial quality is mixed and plain curcumin is poorly absorbed.

paras: Curcumin modulates inflammatory signaling such as NF-κB and COX-2 and has antioxidant activity in laboratory studies. Oral bioavailability is very low because of poor solubility and rapid metabolism, which is why piperine, lipid formulations and other delivery technologies are used.

Generally well tolerated, with occasional gastrointestinal upset. Rare cases of liver injury have been reported with high-bioavailability products, and it may interact with anticoagulants. Supplement quality varies, and adulteration with lead-containing pigments has been documented. Legal as a dietary supplement.
